test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Meristematic tissue is classified into how many types?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meristematic tissues** are a group of young cells that consist of actively dividing cells and are responsible for the **growth and development** of the plant.
 
• Based on their **location or position** in the plant body, these tissues are classified into **three distinct types**: **Apical Meristem**, **Intercalary Meristem**, and **Lateral Meristem**.
 
• **Apical Meristem**: It is located at the **growing tips of stems and roots** (the apices). Its primary function is to increase the **vertical length** of the plant, known as **primary growth**.
 
• **Intercalary Meristem**: These are located at the **base of leaves** or **internodes** (e.g., in grasses). They facilitate the **lengthening of the internode** and help in the regrowth of parts removed by grazing animals.
 
• **Lateral Meristem**: Situated on the **lateral sides** of the plant body, parallel to the longitudinal axis. It is responsible for **secondary growth**, which increases the **girth or thickness** of the stem and root. Examples include **Vascular Cambium** and **Cork Cambium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of Meristematic Cells**:

 
 
• The cells are **immature**, small, and generally **isodiametric** (spherical, oval, or polygonal) in shape.
 
• They possess **thin cell walls** made primarily of **cellulose** and lack **intercellular spaces**.
 
• Each cell contains a **dense cytoplasm**, a **large and prominent nucleus**, and typically lacks **vacuoles** due to high metabolic activity.
 
• These tissues remain in a state of **continuous division** until they differentiate into **permanent tissues**.
 
 
 
• **Other Classifications**:
 
 
• **Based on Origin**: Meristems can also be grouped into **Promeristem**, **Primary Meristem**, and **Secondary Meristem** depending on their developmental stage in the plant life cycle.
